title: Kubernetes operator reconciliation and durable transitions
purpose: Find reachable correctness failures in the Ledger Kubernetes control plane when reconciliation repeats, observations are stale, an external effect commits without a response, or the operator crashes and restarts between durable steps. Cover Cluster, Ledger, Credentials, Backup and BackupRun controllers and their deployed permissions and dependencies. Apply the companion evidence contract; exclude style, performance-only work, generic Kubernetes hardening, and guarantees not established by this repository.
invariants: Repeated reconciliation of the same logical resource must converge under the documented API semantics without duplicating irreversible effects or undoing completed work. Establish logical identity from namespace, name, UID, generation, external operation identity and ownership as applicable; a name reused by a replacement CR is not proof of continuity with the old CR.

Every reported defect must start from an admitted CR or another reachable deployment state and follow the real manager registration, watch/predicate or requeue path, permissions, controller guards and external call to the violated postcondition. A fake-client state forbidden by CRD validation, absent production dependency, or unsupported configuration alone is not evidence of reachability.

Resource creation, adoption, update and deletion must respect controller ownership, namespace and UID boundaries, selectors and retention semantics. Deletion must not recreate resources for a terminating owner or mutate resources belonging to another owner. Finalizers, where used for external cleanup, must survive retries until cleanup is established; garbage collection without a finalizer is valid where it satisfies the declared lifecycle contract.

Status and conditions must describe the observed resource and generation according to their documented meaning. A persisted Ready, Succeeded, applied hash or terminal phase must not falsely certify an unfinished effect or suppress required recovery. Failed status persistence and stale reads must have a reachable convergence path when status is needed for correctness; ordinary temporary observation lag is not itself a defect.

A Kubernetes API write, pod exec, ledgerctl call or backup Job can commit its effect before timing out, losing its response, or failing to persist controller status. Such an error is an unknown outcome rather than proof of no effect. Retry or compensation must establish identity and authoritative postconditions before repeating a non-idempotent effect; do not invent exactly-once guarantees where no contract supplies them.

Backup scheduling, manual BackupRun execution, Job association, result extraction and parent summary updates must preserve the identity and outcome of each execution across conflicts, duplicate events and operator restarts. Success requires the corresponding completed backup result. Run history garbage collection must preserve the documented Kubernetes-history boundary and must not be treated as S3 backup-object retention.

Restore deployment must preserve the intended cluster identity, mode, storage and supplied credentials across reconciles and restarts. Trace the actual handoff between spec.restore, the restore-mode process, external download/finalize commands and the return to normal mode; ordinary readiness or a pod restart must not be taken as proof of completed restore. This is orchestration correctness, not a claim that a Restore controller or automatic restore transaction exists.

Scale-down must establish the required Raft membership removal postcondition before reducing the relevant replicas and disposing of their volumes. An already-absent member and a removal committed before an opaque exec failure must be handled using authoritative membership evidence. Reconciliation after partial removal, changed desired replicas or operator restart must preserve the intended member/node identity and must not destroy still-required storage or bypass documented quorum and force-removal preconditions.

TLS mode transitions, certificate and CA references, cluster secrets and Credentials reconciliation must preserve intended peer connectivity and authorization across rolling updates, rotation, deletion and operator restart. Distinguish desired template state from the mode and keys actually loaded by running pods; an intermediate optional TLS mode is permitted only within the documented transition. Reject unsupported or missing inputs according to established contracts without silently weakening trust or losing ownership of secrets.

Changes to WAL/data PVC size, VolumeClaimTemplates, storage layout and deletion-protection labels must preserve data and resource ownership through the actual supported transition, including orphan/recreate/adopt. Distinguish template request, existing PVC request, bound capacity and mounted filesystem capacity. Do not infer unconditional live expansion or shrink support from a size field, or bypass StorageClass, CSI, admission-policy and retention prerequisites.

After each externally durable step, a fresh operator process with no previous in-memory reconcile state must be able to observe enough evidence to resume, safely compensate, or report an explicit actionable failure under the documented contract. Include crash windows between effects, owner/finalizer writes, status writes and cleanup, plus leader-election handoff. Do not assume an atomic transaction across Kubernetes, Ledger and object storage.

Rollback of a desired-spec change and compensation after partial failure must account for already committed effects. Reverting a CR, cancelling a request, or restoring an in-memory object is not rollback of Raft membership, a backup, a secret write or a PVC deletion. Supported recovery must not resurrect obsolete work or erase unrelated/newer effects; arbitrary downgrade compatibility between unreleased v3 revisions is outside scope.
adversarial_questions: Which reconcilers are registered by the actual manager, with which clients, watches, predicates, namespace restrictions, RBAC and leader-election configuration? Can a dependency change or recovered transient failure trigger another pass without unrelated resource churn?

For each multi-step reconcile, what is changed only in memory, what is committed to the API server, what commits in Ledger or S3, and what residual state remains after every prefix? Which fresh-process observation drives the next action?

Can AlreadyExists, NotFound, a resourceVersion conflict or a lost response refer to a same-name replacement object? Before adopting, mutating, execing into or deleting it, which UID, owner, selector and cluster checks establish the intended target?

What happens when deletion starts between finalizer registration, external ledger/index/credential creation, cleanup and finalizer removal? Are GC and retention policies actually active in the deployed chart, and do they cover cross-scope resources?

Can a status write fail after a successful effect, or a terminal status be persisted before result capture? Does the next pass recover from observed external state, repeat the effect, or skip unfinished work? Is the alleged status failure material to a consumer or convergence?

Can a scheduled run be duplicated or lost between BackupRun creation and parent schedule advancement? What happens when a parent changes, a Job or result pod disappears, multiple Job attempts exist, or a completed run is pruned before the parent observes its result?

Does backup result extraction bind the payload to the right run/Job/pod attempt and type? How are malformed, absent, truncated or stale termination messages and CLI output distinguished from successful backup completion?

During restore, which actor changes mode, downloads, validates and finalizes? What happens if the operator or pod restarts before or after each handoff, or the CR returns to normal mode prematurely? Which readiness signal represents serving state versus management availability?

If one scale-down removal commits and exec returns an opaque error, membership observation is stale or fails, a later removal fails, or the StatefulSet update succeeds before PVC cleanup fails, what happens on retry and after restart? Can a scale-up reversal reuse an old ordinal/PVC or a tombstoned node identity?

When image/config changes coincide with scale-down or TLS migration, which live pod mode, endpoint, CA and token does ledgerctl use? Are intermediate TLS phases reconstructed from actual rollout state after operator restart or a desired-mode reversal?

Do referenced certificate, CA, token and credential changes reach all relevant consumers? Can deletion, failed regeneration, stale caches or a same-name Secret replacement leave an accepted credential active incorrectly, discard a valid key, or point a workload at another owner's secret?

For a PVC growth request, what actually updates the old claims and what only changes templates for future claims? Can orphan deletion succeed before its response is lost, or the operator restart before replacement/adoption, and leave pods, claims, labels or retained data stranded? Is unsupported growth rejected or merely ambiguous in the API contract?

Which retry/backoff and event sources recover after API-server, exec, cert-manager, CSI or object-store availability returns? A transient outage is expected; what concrete mechanism makes the failure permanent, destructive or falsely successful after recovery?

Which tests cross the real production guards and assert final resource UIDs, membership, data, credentials and phase, and which only compare desired manifests or reconstruct an impossible fake state? Can a test pass by reading through another healthy pod while the intended PVC or restored node is wrong?
dynamic_checks_to_consider: Inspect existing operator unit/envtest/Chainsaw cases and their module, API schema, fake-client limitations and assertions first. The audit may run existing checks or allowed temporary diagnostics, but must not edit tracked code, implement new reproducers, or operate a live user cluster; unexecuted scenarios are reproduction plans, not claimed test evidence.

Use an API-server-backed fixture to reconcile an admitted CR twice, inject a conflict or response loss after a successful write, and reconcile with a fresh controller instance; verify external effect count, UID/owner identity and eventual persisted status.

Exercise delete/recreate with the same name and a new UID, delayed child events, terminating owners and failed finalizer cleanup; verify that only the intended resources and external ledger effects are removed.

For scheduled and manual backup runs, interrupt after run creation, Job creation, backup commit, Job completion, result capture and parent summary update; restart the operator and verify run/Job identity, manifest result and Kubernetes-only history retention.

In an isolated existing restore fixture, preserve PVCs across operator and Ledger process replacement around download/finalize/normal-mode handoffs; verify restored sentinel data and cluster identity independently of management readiness, using a non-empty post-checkpoint delta when incremental restore is exercised.

Exercise scale-down with a real fail-then-success sequence: commit removal then lose exec response, fail the postcondition read once, restart between membership removal and replica update, and retry after cleanup failure. Assert membership, replica count, PVC identity and retained data; also reverse the desired scale while work is incomplete.

Interrupt TLS off/optional/required rollouts in both directions, rotate referenced certs/CA/tokens, and restart the operator with mixed pod revisions; verify authenticated peer/CLI connectivity and final phase from actual pod state.

Request WAL/data growth using an explicitly expansion-capable disposable storage fixture, interrupt orphan/recreate/adoption and claim updates, and compare template size, each PVC request/capacity, mounted capacity and a persisted sentinel. Exercise unsupported expansion and deletion-protection/retention configurations separately.

Inject transient API, pod-exec and dependency failures before and after durable effects, restore availability, then assert eventual convergence without unrelated user edits; use deterministic barriers or Eventually assertions rather than sleeps. If envtest, CSI, cert-manager or a separate operator process is unavailable, record that limit explicitly.
